findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows are absent
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. Site settings rows only exist in the `site_settings` table once an admin has changed them, so on the vast majority of installs there is no `embed_category` row (and/or no category whose name matches), the result set is empty, `[0]` is nil and the migration dies with NoMethodError on `nil['id']`, aborting the deploy. The same pattern is repeated on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`, which is a hidden setting that is frequently absent as well. Both queries need an empty-result guard.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted unnormalized (and interpolated unescaped), breaking embedding after upgrade
findings.body: Existing `embeddable_hosts` values could legitimately contain a scheme (the old setting accepted `http://discourse.org`, as the removed SiteSetting spec showed). The migration inserts the raw lines verbatim, so rows like `http://discourse.org` land in `embeddable_hosts.host`. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `URI(referer).host`, i.e. `discourse.org`, so these migrated rows never match and embedding silently stops working for those sites until an admin re-saves each host. The values should be normalized (strip scheme/path/whitespace, including a trailing `\r` from CRLF splits) before insert. Additionally the value is interpolated directly into the SQL string (`'#{h}'`), so a host containing a quote breaks the migration; use a bind/quoted insert.

findings.title: record_for_host compares lower(host) against a non-downcased host
findings.body: `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but `host` comes straight from `uri.host` and is never downcased. A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/post` yields `EvilTrout.com`, which can never equal the lowercased column value, so a legitimately configured host is rejected and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess (and TopicRetriever refuses to retrieve). The comparison value must be `host.downcase`.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `before_validation { self.host.sub!(...) }` assumes `host` is a string. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so a create/update request that omits `host` (or sends null) leaves `host` nil and validation blows up with `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil` — a 500 instead of the intended validation error that the client's `popupAjaxError` expects. Guard with `return if host.blank?` (and prefer non-mutating `sub` so a frozen input string isn't mutated in place).

findings.title: update/destroy 500 when the id does not exist
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id; `save_host(nil)` then calls `nil.host =` and `destroy` (line 16) calls `nil.destroy`, producing a NoMethodError / 500 response. Two admins editing the list concurrently, or a stale browser tab, will hit this. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `find`) so the client gets a proper 404.

findings.title: has_many with embed: :ids does not side-load the hosts the client needs
findings.body: The client hydrates embedded records in `store._hydrateEmbedded`: it sees `embeddable_host_ids` and looks the objects up in `root['embeddable_hosts']`. With ActiveModel::Serializers `embed: :ids` and no `include: true`, only the id array is rendered and no root-level `embeddable_hosts` collection is produced, so `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for every id and `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined`, which the `embedding.hbs`/`embeddable-host` component then renders/mutates. This needs `embed: :ids, include: true` (or `embed: :objects`), and a JS/controller test that actually renders a non-empty host list would catch it.

findings.title: New `_ids` hydration silently drops ids and can throw on non-array values
findings.body: The widened regex `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` now captures every key ending in `_ids`. In the plural branch the original key is deleted unconditionally, even when `root[pluralize(subType)]` is missing: `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` for each id, so the model ends up with e.g. `groups: [undefined, undefined]` and the original `group_ids` data is gone — a silent data loss for any REST-serialized payload (`__rest_serializer === "1"`) that sends id arrays without side-loaded objects. Also `obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError if the serializer sends `foo_ids: null`, and the `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code because `map` always returns an array. Only delete the `_ids` key when the side-loaded collection was actually found, and guard against non-array values.

findings.title: String.replace without /g only converts the first underscore in the type name
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces a single occurrence, so a model type with more than one underscore (e.g. `embeddable_host_group`) will not be matched against `ADMIN_MODELS` and its requests will be sent to `/` instead of `/admin/`, failing with 404/403. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')`.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that reports success
findings.body: `update` only re-renders the freshly-fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct; it ignores the request body entirely. The admin controller's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6`) calls `embedding.update({})` against this route, so the endpoint advertises a write operation and returns 200 while persisting nothing. Either implement the update or drop the route and the client action so no one builds on a fake write API.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid TLDs and ports can never match
findings.body: The format regex caps the TLD at `[a-z]{2,5}`, so legitimate hosts such as `blog.technology`, `example.travel` or `foo.museum` cannot be saved, and `localhost`/bare IPs are rejected too — admins migrating from the old free-form `embeddable_hosts` setting may be unable to re-save their hosts. The regex also permits a `:port` suffix, but `record_for_host` matches against `URI(...).host`, which never includes the port, so a stored `example.com:3000` can never match a referer. There is also no uniqueness validation on `host`, allowing duplicate rows for the same domain.

findings.title: No request specs for the new embeddable host CRUD endpoints
findings.body: The only assertion is that the class inherits from Admin::AdminController. None of create/update/destroy are exercised, so the nil-record 500s in `update`/`destroy`, the nil-host NoMethodError in the model callback, the uncategorized-category fallback, and the serializer shape are all untested. The same applies to `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`. Please add specs that POST/PUT/DELETE as an admin, including the missing-id and missing-host cases.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). It happens to work because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, but the naming is inverted and anyone looking for or editing the category fabricators will not find them where expected. Swap the file contents.

findings.title: Stale test name: expandable_first_post? no longer depends on embeddable hosts
findings.body: `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer asserts what it claims — `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and ignores hosts entirely, so this example passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and the topic has no embed. Either delete the example or rename it to describe what it actually covers, otherwise it gives false confidence that host configuration is still checked.
